source_of_truth: The canonical IAB source file is authoritative. Line citations refer to the helper source file used for structured extraction.

objects.name: BidRequest
objects.description: The top-level bid request object contains a globally unique bid request or auction ID. This id attribute is required as is at least one impression object (Section 3.2.2). Other attributes in this top-level object establish rules and restrictions that apply to all impressions being offered. There are also several subordinate objects that provide detailed data to potential buyers. Among these are the Site and App objects, which describe the type of published media in which the impression(s) appear. These objects are highly recommended, but only one applies to a given bid request depending on whether the media is browser-based web content or a non-browser application, respectively.

fields.name: id
fields.description: Unique ID of the bid request, provided by the exchange.

fields.name: imp
fields.description: Array of Imp objects (Section 3.2.2) representing the impressions offered. At least 1 Imp object is required.

fields.name: site
fields.description: Details via a Site object (Section 3.2.6) about the publisher’s website. Only applicable and recommended for websites.

fields.name: app
fields.description: Details via an App object (Section 3.2.7) about the publisher’s app (i.e., non-browser applications). Only applicable and recommended for apps.

fields.name: device
fields.description: Details via a Device object (Section 3.2.11) about the user’s device to which the impression will be delivered.

fields.name: user
fields.description: Details via a User object (Section 3.2.13) about the human user of the device; the advertising audience.

fields.name: test
fields.description: Indicator of test mode in which auctions are not billable, where 0 = live mode, 1 = test mode.

fields.name: at
fields.description: Auction type, where 1 = First Price, 2 = Second Price Plus. Exchange-specific auction types can be defined using values greater than 500.

fields.name: tmax
fields.description: Maximum time in milliseconds to submit a bid to avoid timeout. This value is commonly communicated offline.

fields.name: wseat
fields.description: Whitelist of buyer seats allowed to bid on this impression. Seat IDs must be communicated between bidders and the exchange a priori. Omission implies no seat restrictions.

fields.name: allimps
fields.description: Flag to indicate if Exchange can verify that the impressions offered represent all of the impressions available in context (e.g., all on the web page, all video spots such as pre/mid/post roll) to support road-blocking. 0 = no or unknown, 1 = yes, the impressions offered represent all that are available.

fields.name: cur
fields.description: Array of allowed currencies for bids on this bid request using ISO-4217 alpha codes. Recommended only if the exchange accepts multiple currencies.

fields.name: bcat
fields.description: Blocked advertiser categories using the IAB content categories. Refer to List 5.1.

fields.name: badv
fields.description: Block list of advertisers by their domains (e.g., “ford.com”).

fields.name: regs
fields.description: A Regs object (Section 3.2.16) that specifies any industry, legal, or governmental regulations in force for this request.

fields.name: ext
fields.description: Placeholder for exchange-specific extensions to OpenRTB.

objects.name: Imp
objects.description: This object describes an ad placement or impression being auctioned. A single bid request can include multiple Imp objects, a use case for which might be an exchange that supports selling all ad positions on a given page. Each Imp object has a required ID so that bids can reference them individually. The presence of Banner (Section 3.2.3), Video (Section 3.2.4), and/or Native (Section 3.2.5) objects subordinate to the Imp object indicates the type of impression being offered. The publisher can choose one such type which is the typical case or mix them at their discretion. However, any given bid for the impression must conform to one of the offered types.

fields.name: id
fields.description: A unique identifier for this impression within the context of the bid request (typically, starts with 1 and increments.

fields.name: banner
fields.description: A Banner object (Section 3.2.3); required if this impression is offered as a banner ad opportunity.

fields.name: video
fields.description: A Video object (Section 3.2.4); required if this impression is offered as a video ad opportunity.

fields.name: native
fields.description: A Native object (Section 3.2.5); required if this impression is offered as a native ad opportunity.

fields.name: displaymanager
fields.description: Name of ad mediation partner, SDK technology, or player responsible for rendering ad (typically video or mobile). Used by some ad servers to customize ad code by partner. Recommended for video and/or apps.

fields.name: displaymanagerver
fields.description: Version of ad mediation partner, SDK technology, or player responsible for rendering ad (typically video or mobile). Used by some ad servers to customize ad code by partner. Recommended for video and/or apps.

fields.name: instl
fields.description: 1 = the ad is interstitial or full screen, 0 = not interstitial.

fields.name: tagid
fields.description: Identifier for specific ad placement or ad tag that was used to initiate the auction. This can be useful for debugging of any issues, or for optimization by the buyer.

fields.name: bidfloor
fields.description: Minimum bid for this impression expressed in CPM.

fields.name: bidfloorcur
fields.description: Currency specified using ISO-4217 alpha codes. This may be different from bid currency returned by bidder if this is allowed by the exchange.

fields.name: secure
fields.description: Flag to indicate if the impression requires secure HTTPS URL creative assets and markup, where 0 = non-secure, 1 = secure. If omitted, the secure state is unknown, but non-secure HTTP support can be assumed.

fields.name: iframebuster
fields.description: Array of exchange-specific names of supported iframe busters.

fields.name: pmp
fields.type_spec: object marketplace deals in effect for this impression.
fields.description: A Pmp object (Section 3.2.17) containing any private

fields.name: ext
fields.description: Placeholder for exchange-specific extensions to OpenRTB.

objects.name: Banner
objects.description: This object represents the most general type of impression. Although the term “banner” may have very specific meaning in other contexts, here it can be many things including a simple static image, an expandable ad unit, or even in-banner video (refer to the Video object in Section 3.2.4 for the more generalized and full featured video ad units). An array of Banner objects can also appear within the Video to describe optional companion ads defined in the VAST specification. The presence of a Banner as a subordinate of the Imp object indicates that this impression is offered as a banner type impression. At the publisher’s discretion, that same impression may also be offered as video and/or native by also including as Imp subordinates the Video and/or Native objects, respectively. However, any given bid for the impression must conform to one of the offered types.

fields.name: w
fields.description: Width of the impression in pixels. If neither wmin nor wmax are specified, this value is an exact width requirement. Otherwise it is a preferred width.

fields.name: h
fields.description: Height of the impression in pixels. If neither hmin nor hmax are specified, this value is an exact height requirement. Otherwise it is a preferred height.

fields.name: wmax
fields.description: Maximum width of the impression in pixels. If included along with a w value then w should be interpreted as a recommended or preferred width.

fields.name: hmax
fields.description: Maximum height of the impression in pixels. If included along with an h value then h should be interpreted as a recommended or preferred height.

fields.name: wmin
fields.description: Minimum width of the impression in pixels. If included along with a w value then w should be interpreted as a recommended or preferred width.

fields.name: hmin
fields.description: Minimum height of the impression in pixels. If included along with an h value then h should be interpreted as a recommended or preferred height.

fields.name: id
fields.description: Unique identifier for this banner object. Recommended when Banner objects are used with a Video object (Section 3.2.4) to represent an array of companion ads. Values usually start at 1 and increase with each object; should be unique within an impression.

fields.name: btype
fields.description: Blocked banner ad types. Refer to List 5.2.

fields.name: battr
fields.description: Blocked creative attributes. Refer to List 5.3.

fields.name: pos
fields.description: Ad position on screen. Refer to List 5.4.

fields.name: mimes
fields.description: Content MIME types supported. Popular MIME types may include “application/x-shockwave-flash”, “image/jpg”, and “image/gif”.

fields.name: topframe
fields.description: Indicates if the banner is in the top frame as opposed to an iframe, where 0 = no, 1 = yes.

fields.name: expdir
fields.description: Directions in which the banner may expand. Refer to List 5.5.

fields.name: api
fields.description: List of supported API frameworks for this impression. Refer to List 5.6. If an API is not explicitly listed, it is assumed not to be supported.

fields.name: ext
fields.description: Placeholder for exchange-specific extensions to OpenRTB.

objects.name: Video
objects.description: This object represents an in-stream video impression. Many of the fields are non-essential for minimally viable transactions, but are included to offer fine control when needed. Video in OpenRTB generally assumes compliance with the VAST standard. As such, the notion of companion ads is supported by optionally including an array of Banner objects (refer to the Banner object in Section 3.2.3) that define these companion ads. The presence of a Video as a subordinate of the Imp object indicates that this impression is offered as a video type impression. At the publisher’s discretion, that same impression may also be offered as banner and/or native by also including as Imp subordinates the Banner and/or Native objects, respectively. However, any given bid for the impression must conform to one of the offered types.

fields.name: mimes
fields.description: Content MIME types supported. Popular MIME types may include “video/x-ms-wmv” for Windows Media and “video/x-flv” for Flash Video.

fields.name: minduration
fields.description: Minimum video ad duration in seconds.

fields.name: maxduration
fields.description: Maximum video ad duration in seconds.

fields.name: protocol
fields.description: NOTE: Use of protocols instead is highly recommended. Supported video bid response protocol. Refer to List 5.8. At least one supported protocol must be specified in either the protocol or protocols attribute.

fields.name: protocols
fields.description: Array of supported video bid response protocols. Refer to List 5.8. At least one supported protocol must be specified in either the protocol or protocols attribute.

fields.name: w
fields.description: Width of the video player in pixels.

fields.name: h
fields.description: Height of the video player in pixels.

fields.name: startdelay
fields.description: Indicates the start delay in seconds for pre-roll, mid-roll, or post-roll ad placements. Refer to List 5.10 for additional generic values.

fields.name: linearity
fields.description: Indicates if the impression must be linear, nonlinear, etc. If none specified, assume all are allowed. Refer to List 5.7.

fields.name: sequence
fields.description: If multiple ad impressions are offered in the same bid request, the sequence number will allow for the coordinated delivery of multiple creatives.

fields.name: battr
fields.description: Blocked creative attributes. Refer to List 5.3.

fields.name: maxextended
fields.description: Maximum extended video ad duration if extension is allowed. If blank or 0, extension is not allowed. If -1, extension is allowed, and there is no time limit imposed. If greater than 0, then the value represents the number of seconds of extended play supported beyond the maxduration value.

fields.name: minbitrate
fields.description: Minimum bit rate in Kbps. Exchange may set this dynamically or universally across their set of publishers.

fields.name: maxbitrate
fields.description: Maximum bit rate in Kbps. Exchange may set this dynamically or universally across their set of publishers.

fields.name: boxingallowed
fields.description: Indicates if letter-boxing of 4:3 content into a 16:9 window is allowed, where 0 = no, 1 = yes.

fields.name: playbackmethod
fields.description: Allowed playback methods. If none specified, assume all are allowed. Refer to List 5.9.

fields.name: delivery
fields.description: Supported delivery methods (e.g., streaming, progressive). If none specified, assume all are supported. Refer to List 5.13.

fields.name: pos
fields.description: Ad position on screen. Refer to List 5.4.

fields.name: companionad
fields.description: Array of Banner objects (Section 3.2.3) if companion ads are available.

fields.name: api
fields.description: List of supported API frameworks for this impression. Refer to List 5.6. If an API is not explicitly listed, it is assumed not to be supported.

fields.name: companiontype
fields.description: Supported VAST companion ad types. Refer to List 5.12. Recommended if companion Banner objects are included via the companionad array.

fields.name: ext
fields.description: Placeholder for exchange-specific extensions to OpenRTB.

objects.name: Native
objects.description: This object represents a native type impression. Native ad units are intended to blend seamlessly into the surrounding content (e.g., a sponsored Twitter or Facebook post). As such, the response must be well-structured to afford the publisher fine-grained control over rendering. The Native Subcommittee has developed a companion specification to OpenRTB called the Native Ad Specification. It defines the request parameters and response markup structure of native ad units. This object provides the means of transporting request parameters as an opaque string so that the specific parameters can evolve separately under the auspices of the Native Ad Specification. Similarly, the ad markup served will be structured according to that specification. The presence of a Native as a subordinate of the Imp object indicates that this impression is offered as a native type impression. At the publisher’s discretion, that same impression may also be offered as banner and/or video by also including as Imp subordinates the Banner and/or Video objects, respectively. However, any given bid for the impression must conform to one of the offered types.

fields.name: request
fields.description: Request payload complying with the Native Ad Specification.

fields.name: ver
fields.description: Version of the Native Ad Specification to which request complies; highly recommended for efficient parsing.

fields.name: api
fields.description: List of supported API frameworks for this impression. Refer to List 5.6. If an API is not explicitly listed, it is assumed not to be supported.

fields.name: battr
fields.description: Blocked creative attributes. Refer to List 5.3.

fields.name: ext
fields.description: Placeholder for exchange-specific extensions to OpenRTB.

objects.name: Site
objects.description: This object should be included if the ad supported content is a website as opposed to a non-browser application. A bid request must not contain both a Site and an App object. At a minimum, it is useful to provide a site ID or page URL, but this is not strictly required.

fields.name: id
fields.description: Exchange-specific site ID.

fields.name: name
fields.description: Site name (may be aliased at the publisher’s request).

fields.name: domain
fields.description: Domain of the site (e.g., “mysite.foo.com”).

fields.name: cat
fields.description: Array of IAB content categories of the site. Refer to List 5.1.

fields.name: sectioncat
fields.description: Array of IAB content categories that describe the current section of the site. Refer to List 5.1.

fields.name: pagecat
fields.description: Array of IAB content categories that describe the current page or view of the site. Refer to List 5.1.

fields.name: page
fields.description: URL of the page where the impression will be shown.

fields.name: ref
fields.description: Referrer URL that caused navigation to the current page.

fields.name: search
fields.description: Search string that caused navigation to the current page.

fields.name: mobile
fields.description: Mobile-optimized signal, where 0 = no, 1 = yes.

fields.name: privacypolicy
fields.description: Indicates if the site has a privacy policy, where 0 = no, 1 = yes.

fields.name: publisher
fields.description: Details about the Publisher (Section 3.2.8) of the site.

fields.name: content
fields.description: Details about the Content (Section 3.2.9) within the site.

fields.name: keywords
fields.description: Comma separated list of keywords about the site.

fields.name: ext
fields.description: Placeholder for exchange-specific extensions to OpenRTB.

objects.name: App
objects.description: This object should be included if the ad supported content is a non-browser application (typically in mobile) as opposed to a website. A bid request must not contain both an App and a Site object. At a minimum, it is useful to provide an App ID or bundle, but this is not strictly required.

fields.name: id
fields.description: Exchange-specific app ID.

fields.name: name
fields.description: App name (may be aliased at the publisher’s request).

fields.name: bundle
fields.description: Application bundle or package name (e.g., com.foo.mygame); intended to be a unique ID across exchanges.

fields.name: domain
fields.description: Domain of the app (e.g., “mygame.foo.com”).

fields.name: storeurl
fields.description: App store URL for an installed app; for QAG 1.5 compliance.

fields.name: cat
fields.description: Array of IAB content categories of the app. Refer to List 5.1.

fields.name: sectioncat
fields.description: Array of IAB content categories that describe the current section of the app. Refer to List 5.1.

fields.name: pagecat
fields.description: Array of IAB content categories that describe the current page or view of the app. Refer to List 5.1.

fields.name: ver
fields.description: Application version.

fields.name: privacypolicy
fields.description: Indicates if the app has a privacy policy, where 0 = no, 1 = yes.

fields.name: paid
fields.description: 0 = app is free, 1 = the app is a paid version.

fields.name: publisher
fields.description: Details about the Publisher (Section 3.2.8) of the app.

fields.name: content
fields.description: Details about the Content (Section 3.2.9) within the app.

fields.name: keywords
fields.description: Comma separated list of keywords about the app.

fields.name: ext
fields.description: Placeholder for exchange-specific extensions to OpenRTB.

objects.name: Publisher
objects.description: This object describes the publisher of the media in which the ad will be displayed. The publisher is typically the seller in an OpenRTB transaction.

fields.name: id
fields.description: Exchange-specific publisher ID.

fields.name: name
fields.description: Publisher name (may be aliased at the publisher’s request).

fields.name: cat
fields.description: Array of IAB content categories that describe the publisher. Refer to List 5.1.

fields.name: domain
fields.description: Highest level domain of the publisher (e.g., “publisher.com”).

fields.name: ext
fields.description: Placeholder for exchange-specific extensions to OpenRTB.

objects.name: Content
objects.description: This object describes the content in which the impression will appear, which may be syndicated or non- syndicated content. This object may be useful when syndicated content contains impressions and does not necessarily match the publisher’s general content. The exchange might or might not have knowledge of the page where the content is running, as a result of the syndication method. For example might be a video impression embedded in an iframe on an unknown web property or device.

fields.name: id
fields.description: ID uniquely identifying the content.

fields.name: episode
fields.description: Episode number (typically applies to video content).

fields.name: title
fields.description: Content title. Video Examples: “Search Committee” (television), “A New Hope” (movie), or “Endgame” (made for web). Non-Video Example: “Why an Antarctic Glacier Is Melting So Quickly” (Time magazine article).

fields.name: series
fields.description: Content series. Video Examples: “The Office” (television), “Star Wars” (movie), or “Arby ‘N’ The Chief” (made for web). Non-Video Example: “Ecocentric” (Time Magazine blog).

fields.name: season
fields.description: Content season; typically for video content (e.g., “Season 3”).

fields.name: producer
fields.description: Details about the content Producer (Section 3.2.10).

fields.name: url
fields.description: URL of the content, for buy-side contextualization or review.

fields.name: cat
fields.description: Array of IAB content categories that describe the content producer. Refer to List 5.1.

fields.name: videoquality
fields.description: Video quality per IAB’s classification. Refer to List 5.11.

fields.name: context
fields.description: Type of content (game, video, text, etc.). Refer to List 5.14.

fields.name: contentrating
fields.description: Content rating (e.g., MPAA).

fields.name: userrating
fields.description: User rating of the content (e.g., number of stars, likes, etc.).

fields.name: qagmediarating
fields.description: Media rating per QAG guidelines. Refer to List 5.15.

fields.name: keywords
fields.description: Comma separated list of keywords describing the content.

fields.name: livestream
fields.description: 0 = not live, 1 = content is live (e.g., stream, live blog).

fields.name: sourcerelationship
fields.description: 0 = indirect, 1 = direct.

fields.name: len
fields.description: Length of content in seconds; appropriate for video or audio.

fields.name: language
fields.description: Content language using ISO-639-1-alpha-2.

fields.name: embeddable
fields.description: Indicator of whether or not the content is embeddable (e.g., an embeddable video player), where 0 = no, 1 = yes.

fields.name: ext
fields.description: Placeholder for exchange-specific extensions to OpenRTB.

objects.name: Producer
objects.description: This object defines the producer of the content in which the ad will be shown. This is particularly useful when the content is syndicated and may be distributed through different publishers and thus when the producer and publisher are not necessarily the same entity.

fields.name: id
fields.description: Content producer or originator ID. Useful if content is syndicated and may be posted on a site using embed tags.

fields.name: name
fields.description: Content producer or originator name (e.g., “Warner Bros”).

fields.name: cat
fields.description: Array of IAB content categories that describe the content producer. Refer to List 5.1.

fields.name: domain
fields.description: Highest level domain of the content producer (e.g., “producer.com”).

fields.name: ext
fields.description: Placeholder for exchange-specific extensions to OpenRTB.

objects.name: Device
objects.description: This object provides information pertaining to the device through which the user is interacting. Device information includes its hardware, platform, location, and carrier data. The device can refer to a mobile handset, a desktop computer, set top box, or other digital device.

fields.name: ua
fields.description: Browser user agent string.

fields.name: geo
fields.description: Location of the device assumed to be the user’s current location defined by a Geo object (Section 3.2.12).

fields.name: dnt
fields.description: Standard “Do Not Track” flag as set in the header by the browser, where 0 = tracking is unrestricted, 1 = do not track.

fields.name: lmt
fields.description: “Limit Ad Tracking” signal commercially endorsed (e.g., iOS, Android), where 0 = tracking is unrestricted, 1 = tracking must be limited per commercial guidelines.

fields.name: ip
fields.description: IPv4 address closest to device.

fields.name: ipv6
fields.description: IP address closest to device as IPv6.

fields.name: devicetype
fields.description: The general type of device. Refer to List 5.17.

fields.name: make
fields.description: Device make (e.g., “Apple”).

fields.name: model
fields.description: Device model (e.g., “iPhone”).

fields.name: os
fields.description: Device operating system (e.g., “iOS”).

fields.name: osv
fields.description: Device operating system version (e.g., “3.1.2”).

fields.name: hwv
fields.description: Hardware version of the device (e.g., “5S” for iPhone 5S).

fields.name: h
fields.description: Physical height of the screen in pixels.

fields.name: w
fields.description: Physical width of the screen in pixels.

fields.name: ppi
fields.description: Screen size as pixels per linear inch.

fields.name: pxratio
fields.description: The ratio of physical pixels to device independent pixels.

fields.name: js
fields.description: Support for JavaScript, where 0 = no, 1 = yes.

fields.name: flashver
fields.description: Version of Flash supported by the browser.

fields.name: language
fields.description: Browser language using ISO-639-1-alpha-2.

fields.name: carrier
fields.description: Carrier or ISP (e.g., “VERIZON”). “WIFI” is often used in mobile to indicate high bandwidth (e.g., video friendly vs. cellular).

fields.name: connectiontype
fields.description: Network connection type. Refer to List 5.18.

fields.name: ifa
fields.description: ID sanctioned for advertiser use in the clear (i.e., not hashed).

fields.name: didsha1
fields.description: Hardware device ID (e.g., IMEI); hashed via SHA1.

fields.name: didmd5
fields.description: Hardware device ID (e.g., IMEI); hashed via MD5.

fields.name: dpidsha1
fields.description: Platform device ID (e.g., Android ID); hashed via SHA1.

fields.name: dpidmd5
fields.description: Platform device ID (e.g., Android ID); hashed via MD5.

fields.name: macsha1
fields.description: MAC address of the device; hashed via SHA1.

fields.name: macmd5
fields.description: MAC address of the device; hashed via MD5.

fields.name: ext
fields.description: Placeholder for exchange-specific extensions to OpenRTB.

fields.name: BEST PRACTICE: There are currently no prominent open source lists for device makes, models, operating
systems, or carriers. Exchanges typically use commercial products or other proprietary lists for these
attributes. Until suitable open standards are available, exchanges are highly encouraged to publish lists
of their device make, model, operating system, and carrier values to bidders.
BEST PRACTICE: Proper device IP detection in mobile is not straightforward. Typically it involves starting
at the left of the x-forwarded-for header, skipping private carrier networks (e.g., 10.x.x.x or
192.x.x.x), and possibly scanning for known carrier IP ranges. Exchanges are urged to research and
implement this feature carefully when presenting device IP values to bidders.

objects.name: Geo
objects.description: This object encapsulates various methods for specifying a geographic location. When subordinate to a Device object, it indicates the location of the device which can also be interpreted as the user’s current location. When subordinate to a User object, it indicates the location of the user’s home base (i.e., not necessarily their current location). The lat/lon attributes should only be passed if they conform to the accuracy depicted in the type attribute. For example, the centroid of a geographic region such as postal code should not be passed.

fields.name: lat
fields.description: Latitude from -90.0 to +90.0, where negative is south.

fields.name: lon
fields.description: Longitude from -180.0 to +180.0, where negative is west.

fields.name: type
fields.description: Source of location data; recommended when passing lat/lon. Refer to List 5.16.

fields.name: country
fields.description: Country code using ISO-3166-1-alpha-3.

fields.name: region
fields.description: Region code using ISO-3166-2; 2-letter state code if USA.

fields.name: regionfips104
fields.description: Region of a country using FIPS 10-4 notation. While OpenRTB supports this attribute, it has been withdrawn by NIST in 2008.

fields.name: metro
fields.description: Google metro code; similar to but not exactly Nielsen DMAs. See Appendix A for a link to the codes.

fields.name: city
fields.description: City using United Nations Code for Trade & Transport Locations. See Appendix A for a link to the codes.

fields.name: zip
fields.description: Zip or postal code.

fields.name: utcoffset
fields.description: Local time as the number +/- of minutes from UTC.

fields.name: ext
fields.description: Placeholder for exchange-specific extensions to OpenRTB.

objects.name: User
objects.description: This object contains information known or derived about the human user of the device (i.e., the audience for advertising). The user id is an exchange artifact and may be subject to rotation or other privacy policies. However, this user ID must be stable long enough to serve reasonably as the basis for frequency capping and retargeting.

fields.name: id
fields.description: Exchange-specific ID for the user. At least one of id or buyeruid is recommended.

fields.name: buyeruid
fields.description: Buyer-specific ID for the user as mapped by the exchange for the buyer. At least one of buyeruid or id is recommended.

fields.name: yob
fields.description: Year of birth as a 4-digit integer.

fields.name: gender
fields.description: Gender, where “M” = male, “F” = female, “O” = known to be other (i.e., omitted is unknown).

fields.name: keywords
fields.description: Comma separated list of keywords, interests, or intent.

fields.name: customdata
fields.description: Optional feature to pass bidder data that was set in the exchange’s cookie. The string must be in base85 cookie safe characters and be in any format. Proper JSON encoding must be used to include “escaped” quotation marks.

fields.name: geo
fields.description: Location of the user’s home base defined by a Geo object (Section 3.2.12). This is not necessarily their current location.

fields.name: data
fields.description: Additional user data. Each Data object (Section 3.2.14) represents a different data source.

fields.name: ext
fields.description: Placeholder for exchange-specific extensions to OpenRTB.

objects.name: Data
objects.description: The data and segment objects together allow additional data about the user to be specified. This data may be from multiple sources whether from the exchange itself or third party providers as specified by the id field. A bid request can mix data objects from multiple providers. The specific data providers in use should be published by the exchange a priori to its bidders.

fields.name: id
fields.description: Exchange-specific ID for the data provider.

fields.name: name
fields.description: Exchange-specific name for the data provider.

fields.name: segment
fields.description: Array of Segment (Section 3.2.15) objects that contain the actual data values.

fields.name: ext
fields.description: Placeholder for exchange-specific extensions to OpenRTB.

objects.name: Segment
objects.description: Segment objects are essentially key-value pairs that convey specific units of data about the user. The parent Data object is a collection of such values from a given data provider. The specific segment names and value options must be published by the exchange a priori to its bidders.

fields.name: id

fields.name: RTB responses contain bids that reference specific impressions within a bid request. Bids are in essence
an offer to buy. The bid response consists of the top-level bid response object and optional objects that
depict the specific bids. An empty HTTP response constitutes a no-bid and is in fact the most bandwidth
friendly form of this signal. A malformed response or a response that contains no actual bids will also be
Following is the object model for the bid response. The top-level object (i.e., in JSON the unnamed
outer object) is denoted as BidResponse in the model. A bid response may contain bids from multiple
“seats” (i.e., the buying entity upstream from the actual bidder). In fact a response may contain
multiple bids from the same seat; typically but not necessarily from different campaigns. This can
improve the seat’s chances of winning since most exchanges enforce various block lists on behalf of
Referring to the figure, the actual response objects are shown on the left, specifically the BidResponse
top level object the seat specific SeatBid collections of Bid objects. The other objects shown are
those objects from the bid request to which response objects related. Specifically, BidResponse
includes the BidRequest ID for positive tracking purposes, and since a request can include multiple
impressions Bid includes the ID of the Imp for which the bid is an offer to purchase. If a bid is made
under the terms of a private marketplace deal, the Bid also includes the ID of the specific Deal object.
Not shown in the model figure is an extensions object. This is an object of undefined structure that can
be added to any other object to convey bidder-specific extensions to the standard. Bidders using these
objects are responsible for publishing their extensions to their exchanges.

fields.name: For each bid, the nurl attribute contains the win notice URL. If the bidder wins the impression, the
exchange calls this notice URL to inform the bidder of the win and to convey certain information using
substitution macros (see Section 4.4) such as the clearing price. The win notice return or the adm
attribute can be used to serve markup (see Section 4.3). In either case, the exchange will also apply the
aforementioned substitution to any macros found in the markup.
Several other attribute are used for ad quality checks or enforcing publisher restrictions. These include
the advertiser domain via adomain, a non-cache-busted URL to an image representative of the content
of the campaign via iurl, an ID of the campaign and of the creative within the campaign via cid and
crid respective, an array of creative attribute via attr, and the dimensions via h and w. If the bid
pertains to a private marketplace deal, the dealid attribute is used to reference that agreement from
The fulfilment of an RTB transaction within the scope of this OpenRTB specification lies in the delivery of
markup. Depending on the impression and other ad type constraints, this markup can be XHTML,
XHTML with embedded JavaScript, a VAST document for video, a Native ad unit structure, and
potentially other formats in the future.
The OpenRTB specification does not require any processing of the ad markup by the exchange other
than macro substitution (refer to Section 4.4) and delivery to the supply-side. There are, however,
multiple standard methods for transferring markup from the bidder to the exchange. The method used
is at the discretion of the bidder, but an OpenRTB compliant exchange is expected to support all
methods as defined in the subsections that follow.
4.3.1 Markup Served on the Win Notice
In this method, ad markup is returned to the exchange is via the win notice. In this case, the response
body of the win notice call (i.e., invoking the bid.nurl attribute) contains the ad markup and only the
ad markup; there must be no other structured data in the response body. Using this method, the
In this method, ad markup is returned directly in the bid itself. This is accomplished via the bid.adm
attribute. If both the adm attribute and win notice return data, the adm contents will take precedence.
Each of the ad serving methods has its own advantages that may be of varying importance to either the
Ad Served on the Win Notice

fields.type_spec: Reduced Bandwidth Costs: Serving ad markup only upon winning can save large amounts of

fields.name: bandwidth usage, the costs for which can be large at high volumes especially for exchanges.

fields.type_spec: Additional Bidder Flexibility: Bidders may typically know the ad they will serve at the time of bid, but

fields.name: this provides an additional optional decision point after the clearing price has been established.

fields.type_spec: Reduced Risk of Forfeiture: A forfeit is the scenario in which a bidder wins, but forfeits due to failure

fields.type_spec: Potential Concurrency: The exchange can choose to return that ad markup and call the win notice

fields.name: The win notice URL and its format are defined by the bidder. In order for the exchange to convey
certain information to the winning bidder (e.g., the clearing price), a number of substitution macros can
be inserted into the win notice URL definition. Prior to calling a win notice URL, the exchange will search
the specified URL for any of the defined macros and replace them with the appropriate data. Note that
the substitution is simple in the sense that wherever a legal macro is found, it will be replaced without
regard for syntax correctness. Furthermore, if the source value is an optional parameter that was not
specified, the macro will simply be removed (i.e., replaced with a zero-length string).
These same substitution macros can also be placed in the ad markup. The exchange will perform the
same data substitutions as in the win notice URL. This occurs irrespective of whether the markup is
returned on the win notice or passed in the bid.adm attribute of the bid response. A use case for
macros in the ad markup might be when a bidder prefers to receive its official win notification from the
device itself. To accomplish this, the bidder would include a tracking pixel in the ad markup, the URL for
which would include any of the available macros.

fields.name: The below is a set of anti-patterns that OpenRTB supporting platforms have observed in various
attempts to implement Deal ID bidding logic.
Subjecting Deal ID Bids to an internal auction on price
The ideal bidding logic describes a process of being liberal about sending bids. Deal ID bids may not be
subject to a classic price auction. There may be an expectation that the buyer and seller want
prioritization to achieve a larger objective: complete delivery of the Deal represented by the Deal ID.
Thus any bidding logic that sorts Deal ID bids by price (with or without open marketplace bids) and
truncates the list too aggressively can endanger the fulfillment of the Deal.
Associating Deal ID to the wrong Object
A Deal ID should be treated as a “targeting token” associated to orders, line-items or campaigns. If the
Deal ID is associated to a Seat/Buyer it may create an undesired application of the Deal ID too many
active campaigns. Alternatively if it is associated to the Advertiser it may limit that entity to only a single
Improper Handling of the Private vs Open Market Flag
The pmp.private_auction flag indicates that the seller is willing or not willing to accept open market
bids (i.e., “all bidders are welcome”). If this flag is not read and interpreted correctly, bid responses may
be invalid. Open market bids sent to a private impression auction may be rejected and should not have
If Seat IDs are treated as a filter of eligible demand partners on an open market impression, this defeats
Silently Applying Margin Discounts to Deal ID Bids
With Deal ID buyers are sellers are communicating directly. The Exchange and Bidder become third-
party automation platforms. If there are any automatic or silent discounts of bid prices (based upon
margins or fees) set by either the exchange or the bidder, then the Deal may fail to function correctly.
